definitions.explanation: A rank of nobility, third in the five-rank peerage system. Equivalent to 'count' in continental European nobility or 'earl' in British peerage. Also used in the former Japanese peerage system (kazoku) established in 1884.

examples.japanese: {伯爵|はくしゃく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{称号|しょうごう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{与|あた}えられた→与える：01821_ataeru⟧。
examples.english: He was given the title of count.

examples.japanese: ドラキュラ{伯爵|はくしゃく}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{有名|ゆうめい}→有名：01106_yuumei⟧な⟦{吸血鬼|きゅうけつき}→吸血鬼：12011_kyuuketsuki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦キャラクター→キャラクター：23518_kyarakutaa⟧だ。
examples.english: Count Dracula is a famous vampire character.

examples.japanese: ⟦{明治|めいじ}{時代|じだい}→明治時代：28080_meijijidai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{華族|かぞく}⟦{制度|せいど}→制度：03291_seido⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{設|もう}けられ→設ける：14220_moukeru⟧、⟦{公爵|こうしゃく}→公爵：17797_koushaku⟧・{侯爵|こうしゃく}・{伯爵|はくしゃく}・{子爵|ししゃく}・⟦{男爵|だんしゃく}→男爵：13585_danshaku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{五|いつ}つ→五つ：02892_itsutsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{爵位|しゃくい}→爵位：18334_shakui⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{定|さだ}められた→定める：10448_sadameru⟧。
examples.english: In the Meiji era, a peerage system was established with five ranks: duke, marquis, count, viscount, and baron.

notes:
One of the five ranks in the Japanese {華族|かぞく} peerage system (1884-1947), modeled after European nobility.

THE FIVE RANKS:
- ⟦{公爵|こうしゃく}→公爵：17797_koushaku⟧ (duke/prince)
- {侯爵|こうしゃく} (marquis)
- {伯爵|はくしゃく} (count/earl)
- {子爵|ししゃく} (viscount)
- ⟦{男爵|だんしゃく}→男爵：13585_danshaku⟧ (baron)

USAGE:
Most commonly encountered in translations of European literature and history (e.g., {伯爵|はくしゃく}モンテ・クリスト — The Count of Monte Cristo) or discussions of Meiji-era Japanese history. The female form is {伯爵|はくしゃく}⟦{夫人|ふじん}→夫人：03597_fujin⟧ (countess).
